headline: V26-3406: make host hooks a first-class part of the workflow

V26-3407.title: Let a skill declare host hooks, and run them through one dispatcher

criteria.text: A manifest matching Decision 2 validates. Each refusal Decision 2 lists has its own row and finding code:
a schema failure;
a duplicate id across the profile;
an unknown event;
a host outside the skill's hosts;
an argv script outside the skill or not among its outputs.

agent-skills hook claude-code stop, run against a fixture generation, produces Claude Code's output for each case below. Every row sends a payload shaped like Claude Code's real Stop payload, with session_id, cwd, hook_event_name and stop_hook_active present, and that key is false unless the row says otherwise.
Single hook: allow, warn and block. The block prints {"decision": "block", ...} with stop_hook_active: false present.
stop_hook_active: true: turns a block into a warn.
Join order: two blocks and a warn. Both block reasons are joined in run order, in a fixture whose run order (sorted skill ids, then manifest order) differs from directory order and catalog order.
Faults: each fault Decision 3 lists, one row each. Each counts as allow, with one stderr line naming the hook. One of these rows also holds a valid block, which still blocks.
Budget: several hooks whose combined run exceeds the overall budget, with the budget constants scaled down in-process.
The dispatcher finishes within the overall budget.
A hook that would start with less than the minimum left is skipped and counted as allow, with its stderr line.
A block from an earlier hook still blocks.
Hosts filter: a hook declaring only codex is neither run nor counted.
No hook: with no hook for the event, the dispatcher prints nothing, exits 0 and starts no process.
Project root: with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset, the dispatcher takes the root from the git top level of the payload's cwd, and the process's own working directory is elsewhere.
No shell: an argv item containing shell metacharacters reaches the hook verbatim.
agent-skills hook claude-code session-start joins context strings in run order, cuts them at 9,000 characters, and prints hookSpecificOutput.
The dispatcher exits 0 in every row, including one where every hook fails.
After a dispatch against a fixture generation whose hook imports a sibling module and starts a Python child, the generation holds no _pycache_ folder and no .pyc file.
The release archive carries agent_skills/hooks.py and schemas/skill-hooks.schema.json, within the entry budget.

V26-3408.title: Install, record and remove Claude Code hook entries with the generation

criteria.text: Install. Installing a generation whose profile declares a stop hook writes exactly the Stop entry of Decision 4. It records hooks in the receipt, and records .claude/ in createdDirectories when it created it. Every other key and entry is equal after parsing, including a user's own entry already in hooks.Stop.
Update, remove and rollback.
Updating to a generation that adds session-start adds only that entry.
Updating between two generations that declare the same events leaves the file byte-identical.
Updating to a generation with no hooks removes both entries, and so does removing a generation. Each follows Decision 4's emptying rule, with one row for each case:
a user entry beside the owned one in hooks.Stop is kept, and parses equal, after the update and, separately, after the removal;
with created true, a user key added after install keeps the file, with that key;
with created false, a file left with only {} is kept;
with created true and nothing else added, the file is deleted.
A rollback restores the prior receipt's entries.

Recovery. A fault is injected at every journal phase, exposing-claude-code-hooks included, between two endpoints that declare different event sets (none, and stop). After recovery, the owned entries equal exactly the events of the receipt recovery commits.
Refusals. Preflight refuses each case Decision 4 lists, one row each and naming the fix:
a non-object file;
a hooks that isn't an object;
an event list that isn't a list;

an altered owned entry. A change to the file between preflight and the rename refuses with exposure-conflict. After that refusal, the file, the receipt and the skill exposures are all the prior endpoint's.
The installed command. Each row runs the exact installed C through sh -c, with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set to the temporary repository:
against an installed hook-bearing fixture generation, it prints the block output;
with .agent-skills/current removed, it exits 1, not 2;
with current naming a generation that has no hook command, it exits 1, not 2.
Reports. plan and diff report hooks.added and hooks.removed. Their other members are unchanged, which the characterization rows pin.

Divergence. status reports local-divergence: hooks when an owned entry is removed, and when one is edited by hand. It reports no divergence after the user adds an unrelated top-level key and their own entry under hooks.Stop.

Adoption. Adopting a skill whose hooks.json declares a claude-code stop hook writes no .claude/settings.json entry and no receipt hooks member. Beside it, a generation install carrying the same skill does write the entry.
Documentation. docs/product-generation.md says what an apply writes to .claude/settings.json, how to remove it, and that downgrading goes through rollback.

V26-3270.title: Make the lead's wait impossible to miss: printed and visible when absent

criteria.text: lead-init, lead-assign, lead-accept and lead-run --resume each print the background lead-wait command, with the right --after, when lanes work or a candidate is queued, and print nothing about it otherwise.
With a lane working and no live lease, the supervisor's "Needs you" and the live view both name the missing listener, and a running lead-wait clears both.
The lease boundary:
a lease whose pid has died counts as absent;
a lease whose updatedAt is 180 seconds old counts as absent;
a lease 179 seconds old with a live pid counts as live;
with a dead pid's lease, the supervisor, the live view and the lease function all report the listener missing.

The guide's "The lead's wake", run-delivery's SKILL.md Lead row and orchestrate-work's Lead authority sentence name lead-wait, and the corpus pins the wording. The hook's own wording belongs to V26-3409.

V26-3409.title: Hold a lead's stop while nobody listens, and orient every session in a delivery

criteria.text: Block. lead-may-stop returns block, with the delivery key and its exact lead-wait command, for a lead checkout with one open delivery, no live lease and mode enforce. There is one row with a lane working and one with a candidate queued. A further row puts the payload's cwd in a subfolder of the lead checkout, and it blocks too.
Modes. It returns warn with the same reason under mode warn, and with the key missing. Under off it returns {"verdict": "allow"} and appends no hook.held.
Allow. It returns {"verdict": "allow"} in each of these cases, one row each:
a live lease;
a lane worktree created under the lead checkout's own .worktrees/;
a lane worktree in a sibling folder;
a folder with no delivery;
a closed delivery;
nothing waiting on the lead.
Lease boundary. A dead pid's lease and a lease 180 seconds old are each treated as absent and return block. A lease 179 seconds old with a live pid returns allow.

Journaling. A block with stop_hook_active: false appends exactly one hook.held, and so does a warn under mode warn. The following stop, with stop_hook_active: true, appends none. An allow appends nothing, and a running wait does not end on hook.held.
Shared checkout. Two open deliveries in one checkout return warn, naming each that lacks a listener, under enforce too.
Orientation. delivery-orient prints Decision 8's fields for a lead and for a lane. It prints {"verdict": "allow"} with no context for any other session and under mode off.
There is one row for each source: startup, resume, clear, compact and fork.
One row checks the 4,000-character cut.

The hostile-text row runs once as the lead and once as the lane. Hostile text is planted in that lane's own story: its journal entries, its hand-off and its tracker title. The same output shows that role's Decision 8 fields present and every hostile string absent.
One row reaches the payload's cwd through a symlink.
doctor.
It refuses an unknown hook id or mode in .agents/run-delivery.json, naming the fix.
It reports, without refusing, when the installed generation's .claude/settings.json lacks the entries the receipt records.
It reports, without refusing, when python3 on PATH is below 3.11.
Through the dispatcher. The hook is run through the shipped dispatcher against a fixture generation, with a real Stop payload carrying stop_hook_active: false.
Its block reaches Claude Code's output as {"decision": "block", ...}.
The second stop, with stop_hook_active: true, comes out as a warn.
Afterwards the fixture generation holds no _pycache_ folder and no .pyc file.
Documentation. references/config.md documents hooks in .agents/run-delivery.json, and the guide documents what each hook does and when it holds a stop.

V26-3410.title: Apply the hooks candidate here and enforce the lead's wait

criteria.text: StandingBinding rows in tests/test_own_deliveries.py pin lead.may-stop: enforce in .agents/run-delivery.json, and pin exactly Decision 4's two entries in the committed .claude/settings.json.
The applied generation is the tagged candidate, and run_delivery.py doctor passes.
The live check is recorded on V26-3406. Each stop's payload and the journal's hook.held count are captured by a logging wrapper that logs stdin and then runs the installed command unchanged:
a claude -p session in a scratch clone with a fixture delivery, held once with the lead-wait command named, appending one hook.held;
a new turn of that session (claude -p --resume) taken while lead-wait runs, which stops freely, with stop_hook_active: false in its payload and no hook.held appended;
a lane session and a session with no delivery, which stop freely;
one interactive resume, which receives the orientation text.

approvals.text: The plan itself, before `lead-setup`. Approving it is the separately approved unit AGENTS.md requires.

approvals.text: Creating the epic and V26-3407 to V26-3410 in Linear from this plan's sections, moving V26-3270 here from V26-3306, and narrowing its title and Scope 3 as Decision 9 says. Done on 2026-11-11.
The minor release candidate's tag, and its apply here in V26-3410.

outOfScope: Codex hooks. Codex documents its own hooks (`.codex/hooks.json`, trusted through `/hooks`), so a Codex adapter is possible, but it is a later unit. V26-3270's "Codex has no equivalent hook" is corrected in the guide (Decision 9), and no Codex file changes.

Any event other than Claude Code's `Stop` and `SessionStart`: no `PreToolUse` guards, no `PreCompact`, no `SubagentStop`, and no lane stop hook. The manifest's event list holds only `stop` and `session-start` (Decision 2), so adding an event is a deliberate change.
Hooks for a single-skill adoption receipt (`adoption` present). Such a generation installs no hooks.
A release-gating host qualifier. The host's behaviour is proven by the recorded live check in V26-3410, not by a qualification record.
`.claude/settings.local.json` and the user's own `~/.claude/settings.json`. The lifecycle writes only the project file (Decision 4).
A final (non-candidate) release. The candidate is promoted at a later batch boundary.

outcome.summary: A skill declares host hooks, the lifecycle installs them, and a lead can't stop while nobody listens.
outcome.text: Skills declare Claude Code Stop and SessionStart hooks run through one dispatcher; the generation lifecycle installs, records and removes their entries in .claude/settings.json; run-delivery ships lead.may-stop and delivery.orient, the lead's wait is printed and its absence shown; and this repository applies the candidate with lead.may-stop enforced.
